title: NASCAR sets format for 2027 Clash at Daytona, 22 drivers eligible
text:

 Mitchell Northam USA TODAY Nov. 18, 2026, 4:53 p.m. ET Hear this story As it has every year since 1979, the 2027 NASCAR calendar will begin with its preseason exhibition race, the Clash.
 Sponsored by Wheatley Vodka, the Clash returns to Daytona International Speedway for the first time since 2021. It was previously held at the Los Angeles Coliseum for three years, then at the historic Bowman Gray Stadium in Winston-Salem, North Carolina, for the past two seasons. The Clash will kick off Speedweeks at Daytona on Saturday, Feb. 13.
 But the Clash will look a bit different this year.
 The non-points race is only open to drivers who won a race or sat on the pole in 2026, previous champions of the Daytona 500 who raced full-time last season, and former Cup Series champions who raced full-time last season. Additionally, Dodge will be granted one original-engine-manufacturer provisional for a full-time driver, which will likely be either AJ Allmendinger or Ty Dillon of Kaulig Racing .
 With that, here are the 22 drivers eligible for the 2027 Clash:
 Christopher Bell (20), Joe Gibbs Racing, Toyota
 Ryan Blaney (12), Team Penske, Ford
 Chase Briscoe (19), Joe Gibbs Racing, Toyota
 William Byron (24), Hendrick Motorsports, Chevrolet
 Ross Chastain (1), Trackhouse Racing, Chevrolet
 Austin Cindric (2), Team Penske, Ford
 Austin Dillon (3), Richard Childress Racing, Chevrolet
 Chase Elliott (9), Hendrick Motorsports, Chevrolet
 Ty Gibbs (54), Joe Gibbs Racing, Toyota
 Denny Hamlin (11), Joe Gibbs Racing, Toyota
 Corey Heim (67), 23XI Racing, Toyota
 Carson Hocevar (77), Spire Motorsports, Chevrolet
 Brad Keselowski
 Kyle Larson (5), Hendrick Motorsports, Chevrolet
 Joey Logano (22), Team Penske, Ford
 Michael McDowell (71), Spire Motorsports, Chevrolet
 Ryan Preece (6), RFK Racing, Ford
 Tyler Reddick (45), 23XI Racing, Toyota
 Ricky Stenhouse Jr. (47), Hyak Motorsports, Chevrolet
 Daniel Suarez (7), Spire Motorsports, Chevrolet
 Shane van Gisbergen (97), Trackhouse Racing, Chevrolet
 TBD entry for Dodge
 While Keselowski is eligible for the Clash — because he won the 2012 Cup Series championship and raced full-time this past season — he has not yet announced his plans for the 2027 season .
 The race is a 70-lap shootout that will feature a competition caution on the 30th lap with a mandatory four-tire change.
 In qualifying for the Clash, NASCAR will allow teams to design their own car. NASCAR will provide teams with specifications — suggesting single car speeds exceed over 200 mph — and then allow teams to use simulation to design it. The car will only be used for qualifying, which will feature a four-tire pit stop with a fueler imitating their task.
 “We heard the fans and they wanted the Clash to make its triumphant return to Daytona,” Frank Kelleher, President of Daytona International Speedway said in a statement. “There is no better way to open Speedweeks than with the Clash under the lights at the World Center of Racing. With qualifying adding another layer of anticipation and a format that delivers high-stakes competition, the Clash will add another must-see event to an already incredible week leading into the Daytona 500.”
 Ryan Preece won the Clash last season at Bowman-Gray Stadium. The 36-year-old from Connecticut then won his first points race at Daytona in July, taking the checkered flag in an overtime finish at the Coke Zero Sugar 400 . The victory propelled Preece into the postseason Chase. The former Whelan Modified Tour champion will drive the No. 6 Ford for RFK this upcoming season.
 Following the Clash, the Duels at Daytona are set for Thursday, Feb. 18. The FedEx Freight Truck Series will race on Friday, then Saturday will feature races for the ARCA Menards Series and O’Reilly Auto Parts Series, and the Daytona 500 is scheduled for Sunday, Feb. 21 with live coverage on FOX.
 Kyle Larson, who captured his third Cup Series championship this season, is still searching for his first career win at Daytona. Tyler Reddick won the Daytona 500 this past season.
